prompt: What retention does a new log group get if nobody sets one?

choices.text: Thirty days
choices.why: Thirty is what the lab set by hand afterwards.

choices.text: Fourteen days, like the free tier
choices.why: There is no default of fourteen; there is no default at all.

choices.text: One day, until a policy is set
choices.why: Nothing is deleted until a policy says so.

choices.text: Never expire
choices.why: Right. Every line stays, and is billed every month.

prompt: The API writes 5 GB of logs a day. At 0.90 USD per GB ingested, what does ingestion cost in a 30-day month?
hint: Gigabytes a month times the price.

prompt: Logs cost 0.90 USD per GB to ingest and 0.0408 USD per GB-month to store. Which change cuts the bill that grows by itself?
hint: One cost is paid once, the other every month.

choices.text: Writing the same lines to two log groups
choices.why: That doubles ingestion and storage alike.

choices.text: Querying the logs less often with Insights
choices.why: Queries are billed apart; they do not make storage grow.

choices.text: A retention policy on the group
choices.why: Right. Storage without retention grows every month; a policy caps it.

choices.text: Moving the group to another region
choices.why: The growth follows the group to any region.

prompt: Why does the shop's API write each request as a JSON object rather than a sentence?
hint: Think of the next person who edits the message.

choices.text: JSON lines are cheaper to ingest
choices.why: Ingestion is billed by size; JSON is usually larger.

choices.text: Queries name fields instead of parsing prose
choices.why: Right. A field survives an edit to the wording; a regular expression does not.

choices.text: CloudWatch refuses lines that are not JSON
choices.why: Any text is accepted; JSON is a choice.

choices.text: JSON lines expire on their own
choices.why: Retention is a property of the group, not of the line format.

prompt: The filter `{ $.status >= 500 }` matched all 300 lines in the lab. What is the right conclusion?
hint: Compare with what the word filter did.

choices.text: moto ignores JSON patterns
choices.why: Right. It applied the plain word and returned everything for the JSON pattern.

choices.text: Every request failed
choices.why: Only a handful had a status of 500 or more.

choices.text: The pattern's syntax is wrong
choices.why: It is valid CloudWatch syntax; AWS would apply it.

choices.text: JSON patterns only work on numbers stored as strings
choices.why: Numeric comparisons work on JSON numbers; that is what they are for.

prompt: `put-log-events` returns `rejectedLogEventsInfo` with events too old. What does that mean?
hint: CloudWatch has a window for timestamps.

choices.text: They were stored and will expire sooner
choices.why: Rejected means not stored.

choices.text: The call failed and nothing was stored
choices.why: The call succeeds; the other events are stored.

choices.text: The retention policy deleted them on arrival
choices.why: Retention deletes stored lines; these never were.

choices.text: Those events were dropped and are not in the group
choices.why: Right. Events older than 14 days are refused, and only this field says so.

prompt: In a Logs Insights query, what does `|` do?
hint: Each command works on the previous result.

choices.text: Separates alternatives, like OR
choices.why: Alternatives go inside a filter; | chains commands.

choices.text: Splits the query across log groups
choices.why: Log groups are chosen when the query starts, not in the text.

choices.text: Pipes one command's result into the next
choices.why: Right. filter, then stats, then sort.

choices.text: Marks a comment
choices.why: It joins commands; it is not a comment.

prompt: Logs Insights costs 0.009 USD per GB scanned. What does one query over 150 GB cost?
An Insights query over a month of logs is too expensive to run every few minutes during an incident. What lowers its cost most?
hint: What decides how much is scanned?

choices.text: A more selective filter command
choices.why: Filtering happens after the scan; the bytes are read anyway.

choices.text: Narrowing the time range
choices.why: Right. The range decides what is scanned, and so what is billed.

choices.text: Adding limit 10 at the end
choices.why: limit cuts the output, not the scan.

choices.text: Sorting by timestamp first
choices.why: Order changes nothing about how much is read.

prompt: Put the commands of the query "which paths fail most" in order.
items: stats count(*) as errors by path
trap: Sorting before stats is the slip: there is no errors field to sort by yet.

prompt: What does a metric filter do with a log line that matches its pattern?

choices.text: Deletes the line to save storage
choices.why: Lines are kept; the filter only reads them.

choices.text: Sends the line to an email address
choices.why: Notifications come from alarms, lesson 10, not from filters.

choices.text: Adds a value to a metric
choices.why: Right. Here, 1 to Shop/Errors5xx for each error line.

choices.text: Copies the line to another log group
choices.why: Copying lines out is a subscription filter's job.

prompt: An alarm watches a metric made by a metric filter. A cleanup removes the log line the filter counts. What happens?
hint: Nothing tells the cleanup that an alarm depended on the line.

choices.text: The filter fails and CloudWatch raises an error
choices.why: A filter that matches nothing is not an error.

choices.text: The alarm switches to the logs automatically
choices.why: Alarms read metrics, not logs.

choices.text: The metric goes quiet and the alarm goes blind
choices.why: Right. With defaultValue 0 it even reports a calm zero.

choices.text: The deployment that removed it is rolled back
choices.why: No alarm fires, so nothing rolls back.

prompt: So that an alarm sees a quiet minute as zero instead of missing data, the metric filter sets `default___=0`.
hint: The value used when no line matches.

prompt: Match each CloudWatch Logs feature to what it is for.

pairs.right: Turning matching lines into a number
Sending lines to another service as they arrive

right_distractors: Encrypting lines with a customer key

prompt: Support wants each customer's request latency for complaints. Where should that live?
hint: Lesson 8 counted what a customer dimension costs.

choices.text: A field in structured logs, queried on demand
choices.why: Right. Billed by the gigabyte, asked only when somebody needs it.

choices.text: A custom metric with a Customer dimension
choices.why: That multiplies metrics by customers, into a huge bill.

choices.text: A dashboard per customer
choices.why: Dashboards draw metrics; it would need the same metrics.

choices.text: A metric filter per customer
choices.why: Each filter feeds a metric, so the count of metrics grows with customers.
